episodes.213782: A complex of thunderstorms produced large hail and high winds across central and northeast South Dakota during the afternoon and evening hours of July 2nd. This tornado damaged multiple machine, grain and livestock trailers at a gravel pit. The tornado also flattened corn and tossed some empty livestock tanks. A second, brief tornado touched down three miles southwest of Willow Lake in Clark County, causing no structural damage.||The largest hail that was measured topped out between 3 inches in diameter 7 miles south southwest of Gann Valley, and baseball sized 7 miles west northwest of Gann Valley. episodes.213945: Warm temperatures combined with sufficient mid level moisture, wind energy, and an approaching weather disturbance to produce scattered showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon of July 1st, especially across portions of the southern Texas Panhandle. Some of these were able to become strong to severe with damaging winds being the primary hazard. Slow movement of storms along with efficient heavy rainfall allowed for some flash flooding to occur.
episodes.214008: Strong thunderstorms moved from southwest to northeast through Garfield and McCone Counties, a few of which became severe.
episodes.214048: Hail, heavy rain, and localized minor flooding occurred in Weld County just after midnight on July 2nd.
episodes.214178: Moist upslope flow across the Rolling Plains was unable to convect for much of the area on the afternoon of the second. This isolated storm over Garza County produced severe wind gusts as it moved over Post (Garza County).
episodes.214186: Shortwaves passing through the southwesterly flow aloft resulted in scattered thunderstorm development on the 1st. One storm managed to produce damaging winds near Study Butte.
episodes.214189: Additional shortwaves in the flow aloft, coupled with upslope flow, resulted in thunderstorm development on the 2nd, especially in and around the higher terrain. One storm managed to produce some wind damage on the east side of Fort Stockton.
episodes.214664: A shortwave moving across the Rockies early on July 2nd produced nocturnal convection across the southern Nebraska panhandle. A few thunderstorms developed, producing strong wind gusts.
episodes.214688: Numerous MCS events during the first few days of July brought a bout of severe weather to Arkansas given their outflow boundaries moving into the state coupled with warming temperatures brought damaging winds to portions of Arkansas within a few severe thunderstorms.
episodes.214753: A trough positioned over the Great Basin in early July saw a weak embedded shortwave ripple through by Utah. With limited moisture, this was sufficient for some isolated convection, and instances of severe wind gusts.
episodes.215495: Isolated thunderstorms developed along a weak frontal boundary during the evening of July 1.  With good low-level acceleration of parcels along the boundary, a weak tornado developed and traveled near Oto, Iowa through the Little Sioux River Valley.
episodes.215496: Scattered storms developed very early on July 2 in response to a 30 to 40 knot low-level jet and up to around 2000 J/kg elevated MUCAPE.  Lift was supplied within a broadly coupled jet entrance region across the western Great Lakes as a wave approached from the central Rockies.
episodes.215497: Scattered storms developed very early on July 2 in response to a 30 to 40 knot low-level jet and up to around 2000 J/kg elevated MUCAPE. Lift was supplied within a broadly coupled jet entrance region across the western Great Lakes as a wave approached from the central Rockies.
episodes.215890: High heat and humidity amid an abnormally warm airmass and ample sunshine made for highly unstable conditions across eastern New York on July 1st and 2nd, 2026. Severe thunderstorms, forced by sufficiently robust mid- to upper-level shortwaves cresting the top of a significant ridge, consequently developed in the mid- to late-evening on both days. On July 1st, convection erupted just after 4 PM and lingered through close to 11 PM. The scattered nature of the storms led to widespread impacts noted in the Adirondacks, Mohawk Valley, Upper-Hudson Valley, Capital District, Mid-Hudson Valley, Taconics, and Mid-Hudson Valley. While some small hail was noted within a few storms, the primary hazard was wind damage. Numerous reports of downed trees and wires were therefore forwarded to NWS Albany. On July 2nd, one cluster of storms in particular developed just before 9 PM, and in reaching severe strength, led to severe tree damage in Columbia County. In fact, the town of Chatham declared a State of Emergency due to the extensive damage that led to more than 40 service calls throughout the overnight. Numerous roads were closed due to blockages from downed trees and wires, many were without power also as a result of downed trees; wires; and damaged transformers, and some in the village even lost water as the water pump station lost power and the backup generator failed. The extent of damage in Chatham led to the determination that this cluster produced winds in excess of 60 mph, with some gusts likely getting as high as 70-90 mph.
episodes.215891: High heat and humidity amid an abnormally warm airmass and ample sunshine made for highly unstable conditions across southern Vermont on July 1st, 2026. A cluster of thunderstorms, forced by sufficiently robust mid- to upper-level shortwaves cresting the top of a significant ridge, consequently developed and tracked through Bennington and Windham Counties late that evening. Reports of wind damage were reported near Putney in Windham County. Several downed trees led to the closure of School House Road a few miles south of the center of Putney.
episodes.215928: Additional clusters of showers and thunderstorms developed along the edges of a high-pressure ridge extending from the Great Lakes and Canada into the northern portions of the region. High dew points and sufficient instability supported scattered thunderstorms that produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.215992: Thunderstorms developed along a surface trough of low pressure, situated across the Nebraska Panhandle and northeastern Colorado during the overnight hours of July 2nd. As  this activity moved into the eastern Nebraska Panhandle, storms became severe. Thunderstorm wind gusts to around 60 MPH were reported in Deuel, Garden and Sheridan Counties.
episodes.216008: During the early morning hours of July 2, 2026, widely scattered thunderstorm development occurred across eastern Nebraska as warm air advection was directed into the region. While ample instability was in place, bulk shear remained weak, preventing storms from becoming highly organized or long-lived. However, one storm that tracked from Saunders into Dodge County produced hail measured up to 1.00 inch in diameter at 2:55 AM CST. Based on radar trends, the storm weakened shortly thereafter.
episodes.216063: A severe thunderstorm occurred in Cassia County.

episodes.216274: A hot and humid airmass  was in place across the region with scattered thunderstorms developing during the afternoon and evening hours. A few of these thunderstorms producing damaging winds and hail up to the size of quarters.
episodes.216366: A cluster of thunderstorms moved northeast across portions of east-central and northeast Colorado during the late evening hours on the 1st. A wind gust of 64 mph was measured just south of Burlington.
episodes.216489: High based thunderstorms in Baca County went on to produce gusty winds, with some winds reaching up to 60 mph.
episodes.216621: During the late evening hours on the 1st, a small cluster of thunderstorms moved north to northeast over portions of far southwest Nebraska. One inch diameter hail was reported in Dundy County.
episodes.216644: During the evening hours on the 1st, a few clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms moved northeast across portions of northwest Kansas. Up to two inch diameter hail was reported in Thomas County, and a 61 mph wind gust was measured in Decatur County.
episodes.216693: The weak shortwave that caused thunderstorms across northeast Mississippi the previous afternoon pushed northwest into Middle Tennessee on July 2, 2026.  Afternoon storms developed over Middle Tennessee, feeding on an unstable airmass that featured steep mid-level lapse rates in excess of 8 C/km and SBCAPE values over 3500 J/kg. Storms traveled west into West Tennessee producing several reports of damaging winds and isolated large hail through the early evening hours.
episodes.216704: During the evening hours on July 1st a brief EF-0 tornado damaged a grove of trees near Stacyville. This tornado was observed by several storm spotters in the area.
episodes.216712: A volatile air mass with up to 3000-4000+ J/kg MLCAPE and 30 to 40 knots of deep layer shear developed by early afternoon over south central and parts of southeast South Dakota. Moisture pooled near a convectively enhanced outflow boundary from overnight convection, and stronger heating toward south central South Dakota broke the cap by early afternoon near enhanced convergence near Chamberlain. Initial cells were very slow moving and isolated, leading to longer-lived intense updrafts. By late afternoon, storms evolved into a broken linear structure as convection entered southwest Minnesota.
episodes.216720: During the late evening hours on July 1st, a line of storms moved through west-central Wisconsin and produced isolated wind damage. Additionally, a bowing segment in the line produced a brief EF-1 tornado which damaged trees and some infrastructure in Adams County.
episodes.216751: Onshore flow in place supported sufficient moisture influx resulting in scattered morning showers and thunderstorms over the coastal waters on July 2nd. With little organized large-scale forcing and generally light winds, localized convergence beneath developing showers provided a favorable environment for waterspouts. A weak waterspout was observed near South Pass followed by another one over Lake Borgne south of Lake Catherine in the morning hours.
episodes.216828: During the early morning hours on July 2nd, repeated rounds of thunderstorms over portions of southeast Minnesota resulted in instances of flash flooding. This included a closure of Interstate 90 in Mower County due to flooding.
episodes.216836: During the afternoon hours on July 2nd, severe storms moved across portions of northeast Iowa where they produced strong wind gusts and large hail. One storm in particular produced very large hail in Fayette County where there were reports of baseball sized hail or larger.
episodes.216838: Severe storms moved from northeast Iowa into Grant County where several instances of severe hail and wind gusts were reported. Most notably, a 78 mph wind gust was observed at the AWOS at Platteville Airport.
episodes.216872: Scattered thunderstorms developed along the coast during the afternoon of July 2nd. A waterspout was spotted from a storm over the north end of Sabine Lake.
episodes.216873: The Storm Prediction Center highlighted parts of Western New York under a Marginal to Slight Risk for severe weather on July 1st, citing an unstable air mass ahead of an approaching cold front. NWS Buffalo's Area Forecast Discussions noted that daytime heating in the 80s combined with pooling dew points near 70��F to generate moderate surface-based instability across the CWA. Convection initialized along early afternoon lake breeze boundaries before organizing into multi-cell line segments along the primary frontal boundary. As storms moved west to east, the primary hazards observed across the Finger Lakes and Eastern Great Lake regions were localized damaging wind gusts along with isolated heavy downpours.

episodes.217315: Severe weather impacted northern New Hampshire, primarily Coos, Grafton, and northern Carroll counties during the late afternoon and early evening hours of July 1st.   A mid-level shortwave trough and associated pre-frontal trough moved east-northeast out of northern Vermont into northern New England. An unseasonably hot and muggy airmass ahead of the boundary yielded strong storm based CAPE, supporting organized multicell clusters and short bowing segment thunderstorms that caused isolated wind damage.
episodes.217316: During the late evening hours of July 1st, a cluster of severe storms developed along a leeside low pressure area near the Colorado-Kansas line in a very warm, moist air mass. episodes.217320: Weak mid-level shortwave energy moved east-northeast out of VT provided a trigger during peak afternoon heating with a heat ridge impacting the region. One storm was able to realize the low level instability and became severe with large hail and gusty winds.
episodes.217326: A very warm and unstable atmosphere, combined with slow-moving upper level disturbance within a weak southwest-flow aloft environment, fostered the development of slow-moving strong to severe thunderstorms which resulted in several damaging thunderstorm wind gusts, large hail, and flash flooding across mainly far southwest Kansas.

The tornado traveled north through the cemetery where several headstones were toppled and damage was done to tree limbs. This tornado moved out of Buffalo County and entered Jerauld County around one-half mile north of 233rd Street around 3 miles east-southeast of Gann Valley. The tornado continued northeast across open areas of western Jerauld County before it lifted around one mile west of Spring Valley Colony.  The tornado could not be rated (EFU) due to a lack of damage indicators. The tornado path end and average path width of 20 yards in Jerauld County was estimated based on chaser observations.

Water was observed across several roads, including near the junction of 303rd Ave and 218th St, and parts of Highway 1806 in southeast Stanley County. Water was also forced out of its banks along LaRoche Creek.

The tornado was witnessed by several storm chasers as it developed just north of 229th Street around 4 miles northeast of Spring Valley Colony. The tornado tracked northeast in an open area along a creek for around one-half mile before it crossed South Dakota Highway 34. The tornado continued northeast for a couple more minutes before it crossed 368th Avenue.  The tornado dissipated about a minute later just east of the end of 227th Street. The tornado could not be rated (EFU) due to a lack of damage indicators. The average path width based on video was around 20 yards.

Spotters observed a tornado develop a little over one-half mile west of Dakota Avenue North, just south of U.S. Highway 14. Shortly after touchdown, the tornado damaged an outbuilding. Intermittent ground contact was noted by spotters as the tornado tracked eastward just to the south of U.S. 14 with minimal additional damage. The tornado dissipated just east of Custer Ave. NE. The tornado was rated EF1 with an estimated peak wind of 90 mph. The average path width for the tornado was 50 yards.

Public videos relayed via broadcast media showed a brief circulation determined to be associated with a landspout tornado near the intersection of Colonial Blvd and Interstate 75. Footage initially showed the circulation traversing the parking lot of a Target retail store located on Dynasty Drive east of Interstate 75, before crossing the interstate where additional footage showed the circulation along Colonial Blvd just west of the intersection with Interstate 75. A few shopping carts were tossed in the parking lot of the store along with some tree foliage, with additional mostly minor debris seen briefly lofted as the circulation moved across Colonial Blvd. No significant damage was observed.
